$comment: Rung 1 of the trust ladder: hand-verified values that beat every automated source. Every row with `vendorVerified` carries the `verifiedUrl` that was actually read, and the date it was read — that is what makes the claim checkable rather than merely asserted. Verification passes, what each covered and what each could NOT reach are recorded in `$verificationPasses` below; that is the field to read before assuming a row was checked. `capabilityIndex` is an illustrative 0-100 placeholder used only for the value map's Y axis - it is NOT a benchmark score, models without one are simply not plotted, and the UI says so.
$displayNames: Some entries carry a `displayName` and nothing else. Those are NOT price claims — they deliberately omit `vendorVerified`, so the rate and its provenance keep coming from whichever source the trust ladder chose. They exist because upstream ids get title-cased into names like `GPT 5`, `O3 Mini` and `Qwen3 Vl 235b A22b Instruct`, and since every model now has a public page those strings are its <h1> and its search-result title. A name is presentation; correcting one must not quietly upgrade a price to `vendor`.
$coverage: The catalog tracks what the automated feed carries. Vendors ship models before LiteLLM catalogues them — Z.ai published GLM-5.2 and GLM-5-Turbo on 2026-08-02 while the feed had neither — and the deliberate answer is to wait rather than hand-add. An override with a full `pricing` block CAN create a model the feed lacks, but that price is then frozen: no feed row exists to correct it, so it silently rots. Seeding from OpenRouter instead would publish a reseller's price as the vendor's, which for these providers runs 20-50% adrift. Missing a model for a few days costs less than publishing a number that is wrong and cannot self-correct. New models arrive on their own the morning the feed catches up.
$scope: These are standard-tier, global-endpoint list prices in USD. Not modelled: regional/data-residency premiums (OpenAI and Anthropic both charge 1.1x), fast/priority tiers, server-side tool call fees, fine-tuning, and negotiated volume discounts. The UI states this boundary rather than implying the figure is a whole invoice.
$timeOfDay: DeepSeek V4 publishes peak and off-peak rates but the current schema has no time-of-day tier. PromptSpend uses the higher peak rate so an estimate cannot silently understate the bill; off-peak usage can cost 50% less. Revisit this conservative representation when the engine can model a schedule explicitly.
$verificationPass20260812: First-party rendered pricing tables cleared four standing feed-versus-reseller flags without freezing matching base rates: Qwen 3.7 Max at the International/Singapore rate, Qwen3 Next 80B Instruct, Qwen3 VL 235B Instruct, and MiniMax M2.5. MiniMax also publishes a $0.375/M prompt-cache write rate absent from the feed; that modifier alone is overridden. This evidence was reconciled into the current catalog on 2026-08-16 from the reviewed PR #65 rather than merging its stale generated artifacts.

models.$note: The intro block was flattened away on 2026-08-16 (commit a43fcc6) and restored on 2026-08-20. The list price is $3/$15; $2/$10 is introductory and ends 2026-08-31. Recording the in-force rate as THE price is the specific trap here: it reads correct on the day it is written, the weekly audit still says `agree` because LiteLLM lags the same way, and the row then silently understates by 33% from the moment the window closes. An intro rate must always be written as `intro` + `until`, never as the base `pricing`.

OpenAI documents that the bare `gpt-5.6` id routes to GPT-5.6 Sol. Marking it an alias keeps one purchasable model from appearing twice in the picker and twice on the value map; the row stays in the catalog table so anyone searching for the id still finds it.

Read on 2026-08-26. OpenAI’s pricing page now prints $4/$0.40/$5.00/$20 short-context and $8/$0.80/$10/$30 long-context for gpt-5.6-sol, and states: "GPT-5.6 Sol’s promotional pricing is available at least through November 21, 2026." Those are promotional rates, not a repricing, so per the rule recorded on claude-sonnet-5 they go in `intro` and the list price stays as `pricing`. The list price is not reprinted on the page, but every promotional figure is exactly a uniform 20% off input and 33% off output of the recorded list set — 5→4, 30→20, 0.5→0.4, 6.25→5, 10→8, 45→30, 1→0.8, 12.5→10 — all eight reconcile, which is what confirms $5/$30 is still the correct base. Note "at least through": the window may be extended, so treat 2026-11-21 as a floor and re-read before it lapses. Schema limit: `intro` carries no long-context variant, so the promotional $8/$30 long-context tier cannot be expressed and `longContext` still shows list. This row stays flagged as `override-drift` by design — the feed reports the promotional $4/$20 while the base is $5/$30, exactly as it does for claude-sonnet-5.

Read against Moonshot's own per-model page on 2026-08-22, the morning the daily sync discovered this model by pattern match and published it straight from the feed. All four published fields match that page exactly - $3.00 input on a cache miss, $15.00 output, $0.30 on a cache hit, and a 1,048,576-token context window - so this row records provenance ONLY and its rate keeps flowing from the feed, the same treatment K2.5 gets. Worth writing down because the numbers invited suspicion rather than allayed it: $3/$15 is also Claude Sonnet 5's rate, which is exactly what an unfilled LiteLLM placeholder would look like. It is not one - the vendor's own table prints those figures. No capabilityIndex is recorded here. The field is illustrative and picking a value to get the flagship onto the value map would dress a guess as a measurement, so K3 stays off the chart and in the table until somebody places it deliberately.

Read against Moonshot's own per-model page on 2026-08-19. All three published fields match the feed exactly - $0.60 input on a cache miss, $3.00 output, $0.10 on a cache hit - so this row records provenance ONLY and its rate keeps flowing from the feed. Its openrouter-disagreement flag is expected to survive this and is correct: a provenance-only override does not supply a base price, so the cross-check still runs, and OpenRouter's $0.45/$2.25 is a reseller-routed price - the same structural gap already documented on K2.6. This CORRECTS the 2026-08-09 conclusion that K2.5 was unverifiable because the vendor's pricing index no longer lists it. The index is not the whole site: /docs/pricing/chat-k25 still exists and still renders a full price table, it is merely unlinked now that K3, K2.7 Code and K2.6 occupy the index. Worth keeping as a general rule - a model vanishing from a vendor's index is not evidence its pricing page is gone; try the per-model URL pattern directly before recording something as unreadable. Re-read on 2026-08-22 while verifying K3: the table still prints $0.10 / $0.60 / $3.00 over 262,144 tokens, unchanged, so lastVerified moves and nothing else does.

Read on 2026-08-26 in the Singapore/International section of the Model Studio pricing page, which prints "List price $2.5 / Limited-time 50% off" for input and "List price $7.5 / Limited-time 50% off" for output. The list price is what is recorded here. The 50% discount is deliberately NOT written as `intro`: Alibaba states no end date for it anywhere on the page, and `intro` requires `until` — inventing a deadline would be fabricated provenance. Consequence: while the promotion runs, this row overstates the in-force rate by 50%. That is the safe direction to be wrong, but it is wrong; if Alibaba ever publishes an end date, add `intro` at $1.25/$3.75 with that date. Separately, the per-model page /model-studio/qwen3-7-max shows $1.65/$4.951 — that is the China/Global regional rate, NOT the International (Singapore) rate this catalog uses, so it must not be copied here. That page has no International table at all, which is why the earlier verification against it never settled anything.

Read on 2026-08-26: the Model Studio pricing page lists qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct (International/Singapore, non-thinking) at $0.15 input / $1.2 output per 1M tokens, matching what was already published. The numbers are written out explicitly rather than left to the feed because a bare `vendorVerified` does NOT silence the OpenRouter cross-check — that check only stands down when the override supplies a base price. OpenRouter resells this at $0.1/$1.1; the gap is its own routing margin, not a vendor repricing.

Read on 2026-08-26: the Model Studio pricing page lists qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruct (International/Singapore, non-thinking) at $0.4 input / $1.6 output per 1M tokens, matching what was already published. Written out explicitly for the same reason as the sibling Qwen row — `vendorVerified` alone does not stand the OpenRouter cross-check down, only a supplied base price does. OpenRouter resells at $0.21/$1.9, which is its own margin rather than a vendor move.
MiniMax lists M2.5 under Legacy Models. Input, output, and cache-read rates match the feed, so they remain feed-driven; only the vendor-published cache-write modifier is overridden.

$verificationPasses: 2026-08-01: Anthropic and OpenAI flagship rows read against the first-party pricing pages; all matched the automated feed, and the additions were the modifiers the feed does not carry (cache writes, long-context tiers, batch discounts). 2026-08-03: a second pass covering 27 more rows across Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI and DeepSeek. Every one of the 27 matched the feed exactly, so these entries record provenance ONLY — no `pricing` block — which leaves the rate flowing from the feed and self-correcting. Recording a price we did not need to change would freeze it for no reason. NOT verifiable on 2026-08-03, and deliberately left as `litellm`: Mistral Large 3 and Medium 3.5, Command A, all four Kimi rows, all four MiniMax rows and GLM-5-Code are absent from their vendors' own pricing pages; Gemini 3 Pro Preview, Grok 2/3/4/4.1-fast and DeepSeek R1/V3/V3.2 are not listed on the pages that carry their siblings. An aggregator would have numbers for all of them, which is exactly why this catalog does not accept one. 2026-08-09: Kimi K2.6 read against Moonshot's own per-model pricing page and moved to `vendor`. The 2026-08-03 pass recorded it as not verifiable because no such page existed; the platform has since moved from platform.moonshot.ai to platform.kimi.ai and now publishes a page per model. The vendor's figures match the feed exactly — $0.95 input on a cache miss, $4.00 output, $0.16 on a cache hit — so this row records provenance ONLY and its rate keeps flowing from the feed. That also settles the standing cross-source flag on it: OpenRouter's $0.58/$2.44 is a reseller-routed price, the 20-50% adrift case `$coverage` describes, and the published number was the right one all along. NOT verified in this pass and deliberately still `litellm`: Kimi K2.5 and K2-thinking, which the vendor's pricing index no longer lists — it now carries K3, K2.7 Code, K2.6 and the sunsetting Moonshot V1. The vendor publishes K3 and K2.7 Code, which the feed does not yet carry; per `$coverage` those are left to arrive on their own rather than hand-added.
